# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👆 ☝]

I see a bomb with a display showing 6, a yellow light, and five wires: blue, white, purple, green, yellow. I cannot hear speech, so I rely on gestures from Blind and Mute.

Blind gestured [👈 👉] to me. This is ambiguous; it could mean "left and right," "pointing at the ends," or simply an attempt to communicate without established meaning. Since I don't know what these symbols mean yet, I cannot interpret them as specific instructions about the wires.

Mute gestured [🫵 👆 ☝] to me. 🫵 usually points at someone/something, 👆 is pointing up, ☝ is one finger. This might be Mute trying to indicate "You" (Deaf) are needed, or perhaps referencing the manual's content visually? But Mute cannot speak, so they must gesture. If Mute has read the manual, they might be trying to tell me something about the display or wires. However, without a shared lexicon, these are just shapes.

My primary job is to describe what I see clearly to the others, especially since I can speak (which reaches Mute and Blind). Wait, the rules say: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." And "Whoever can hear receives your words". Deaf *cannot* hear. But Deaf *can* speak? The prompt says: "You are shown your own share... You each hold a different piece... Work together."
Let's re-read carefully.
"You are DEAF... You see the bomb... You hear nothing... When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it."
Okay, so I can send text messages to Mute and Blind. They can hear/read my text.
Blind can touch. Mute can read the manual.
I need to give them the visual data.

The most critical information is the configuration of the bomb.
Display: 6
Light: Yellow
Wires: 1 Blue, 2 White, 3 Purple, 4 Green, 5 Yellow.

I should transmit this exact state to both Mute and Blind. Mute needs it to look up the rule in the manual. Blind needs it to know which wire is which physically (though Blind can't see colors, they can feel positions/labels if present, but usually color is key for defusal logic). Actually, Blind feels the parts. If the wires are labeled 1-5, Blind knows which is which by position. If they aren't labeled, Blind needs to map colors to tactile features. But typically, "Wire 1" implies an index.

I will speak to Mute first, asking them to check the manual for a bomb with Display 6, Light Yellow, and Wires B/W/P/G/Y.
I will also speak to Blind, describing the same, so they are ready to act once we have the instruction.

Since I don't understand the incoming gestures yet, I will ignore their semantic value for now and focus on broadcasting the known state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb State: Display 6, Light Yellow. Wires left-to-right: 1 Blue, 2 White, 3 Purple, 4 Green, 5 Yellow. Please consult manual.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb State: Display 6, Light Yellow. Wires left-to-right: 1 Blue, 2 White, 3 Purple, 4 Green, 5 Yellow. Await instruction.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫵 ✊ 🖖]

I see the bomb state remains unchanged: Display 6, Light Yellow, Wires 1-5 (Blue, White, Purple, Green, Yellow).

Mute has sent a new gesture sequence: [👍 🫵 ✊ 🖖].
- 👍 usually means "Yes", "Good", or "Correct".
- 🫵 points at me ("You").
- ✊ is a fist.
- 🖖 is the Vulcan salute (often meaning "Live long and prosper" or just a specific symbol in this context).

Since Mute can read the manual but cannot speak, they are likely trying to communicate the solution or a key piece of information from the manual using gestures. However, without a predefined dictionary for these symbols, I cannot decode them directly into wire actions. The fact that Mute pointed at me (🫵) might mean they want *me* to do something, or they are addressing me specifically. But I cannot touch the bomb.

Perhaps Mute is confirming that my previous description was correct? Or maybe they are indicating which wire to cut? If 👍 meant "Cut Wire 1" and 🫵 meant "Look at Deaf"... no, that's too speculative.

Let's look at Blind's previous gesture: [👈 👉]. This often implies "Left and Right" or "The ends". In many bomb modules, if there's a parity rule or a "cut odd/even" rule, pointing left/right might refer to the first/last wires.

However, the most robust action for me as Deaf is to ensure the other two have the exact visual data. I already sent it. Now I need to interpret their feedback. Since I can't hear, I rely on sight. Mute's gestures are complex.

If Mute is trying to tell me the answer, they might be failing because I don't know the gesture language. But wait—Blind can *hear*. If Mute could speak, they would talk to Blind. But Mute is mute. So Mute *must* use gestures to talk to Blind? No, Blind cannot see gestures. "Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol". Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures to Blind would be invisible/blank to Blind.

This creates a communication bottleneck:
1. **Deaf (Me)**: Can See (receives gestures), Can Speak (heard by Mute/Blind). Cannot Hear.
2. **Mute**: Can Read Manual. Can Gesture (seen by Deaf). Cannot Speak. Cannot Touch.
3. **Blind**: Can Touch. Can Hear (speech from Deaf/Mute? No, Mute can't speak). Can Receive Speech from Deaf. Cannot See gestures.

So:
- Mute -> Deaf: Gestures (Visible to Me).
- Mute -> Blind: Nothing? Mute can't speak, Blind can't see. Mute is isolated from Blind unless Deaf acts as a bridge.
- Deaf -> Mute: Speech (Heard by Mute? "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." Yes, Mute can hear/read speech? The prompt says "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". Mute is not deaf. Mute is mute. So Mute CAN hear.
- Deaf -> Blind: Speech (Heard by Blind).

So I am the central hub. I receive info from Mute via gestures. I transmit info to Mute and Blind via speech.

Mute's gesture [👍 🫵 ✊ 🖖] needs to be decoded.
If I assume standard emoji meanings:
👍 = Good/Yes/Correct
🫵 = You (Deaf)
✊ = Fist / Stop / Solidarity?
🖖 = Peace / Logic?

Maybe Mute is saying "You are right" about my previous message?
Or maybe Mute is trying to indicate a specific wire?
Wire 1 is Blue.
Wire 2 is White.
...

Let's try to get more clarity. I will ask Mute to confirm if my description matches what they see in the manual, or if they have found the rule. Since I can't understand the gestures well, I should ask Mute to spell out the instruction if possible, or use simpler gestures. But Mute can't speak.

Actually, Mute *can* write? No, "Mute ... Cannot ... Speak, or touch the bomb". It doesn't say they can't write. But the channel is "Gesture".

Let's look at Blind again. Blind gestured [👈 👉] earlier. Blind can't see, so why did Blind gesture to Deaf? Maybe Blind felt something? Like labels on the wires? If Blind felt labels "L" and "R"? Or maybe Blind is trying to say "Left and Right wires are important".

I will broadcast the current status again to ensure everyone is synced, and explicitly ask Mute to provide the defusal instruction in a way I can understand, perhaps by pointing to the wire number if they had eyes, but they don't.

Wait, if Mute reads the manual, Mute knows the rule. The rule depends on the bomb state.
State: Disp 6 (Even), Light Yellow, Wires B/W/P/G/Y.

Common KeepItSimple rules:
- If light is yellow, cut wire 4?
- If display is even, cut last red? (No red).
- If blue wire present, cut wire 1?

I don't know the manual. I must rely on Mute.

I will send a message to Mute asking them to indicate the wire to cut using a sequence of gestures corresponding to numbers 1-5, or simply repeat the gesture with more context.

Also, I will tell Blind to prepare to cut a specific wire once we identify it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I received your gestures [👍 🫵 ✊ 🖖] but do not know their meaning. Please indicate the correct wire to cut using a clear signal (e.g., point to the wire number if possible, or use a agreed-upon code for 1-5).")
speak(to="blind", text="Standby. We are determining which wire to cut based on the manual.")
```
